messages:
Alex P: quick heads-up: spotted a 6-9% tail latency bump on long-seq workloads after the kernel-selector change in 2.3.
Mira T: saw that in perf dashboards too. looks correlated with seqlen > 1024 and a fallback to the small-tile path. :thinking:
Jonah R: interesting — which fallback? the reg-conservative path or the smem-constrained one?
Alex P: smem-constrained. selector is moving certain kernels to the low-smem tile that increases per-token launching overhead for large kv state.
Mira T: dev profile shows higher register spill for the fallback kernel. stacktrace points to liveness pass inasm/ops.
Jonah R: can we push a quick experiment: force the high-occupancy kernel for seqlen 2048 and measure? should be cheap to flip in the routing table.
Alex P: doing that now. toggled routing flag: 
```
kernel_routing[model_family="longseq"] = {
  threshold_seqlen = 1500,
  prefer_high_occupancy = true,
  max_smem_bytes = 110000
}
```
CI-bot: experiment job queued: perf/longseq/forced-highocc/2248883331 (ETA ~12m)
Mira T: while that's running, quick note: our autotune still biases by peak occupancy alone. we might need a composite metric: effective_smem_per_thread + reg_spill_risk. occupancy alone hides launch/kv overhead.
Jonah R: +1. propose metric: score = occ*0.6 - spill_risk*1.2 + kv_prefix_penalty*0.8. tune weights later.
Alex P: experiment results: forced-highocc reduced 99p latency by 7.4% and decreased token-cost by ~3.1%. better than the fallback.
Mira T: nice. curious about memory headroom though — any OOMs?
Alex P: none on A100-80GB infra. memory margin went down ~8% but stable.
Sreisha: does this mean selector should prefer high-occupancy kernels for seqlen > 1500? want to flag for canary rollout.
Mira T: probably yes, but we should add a safety check for devices with <40GB memory. fallback for small cards.
Jonah R: also add a liveness/reg-pressure heuristic — if predicted register usage > 60% then avoid high-occupancy.
Alex P: sketching the patch:
```patch
- if (seqlen > S) pick(low_smem_kernel)
+ if (seqlen > S && device_mem >= 40GB && predicted_regs < 0.6) pick(high_occ_kernel) else pick(low_smem_kernel)
```
Mira T: let's gate by model tag too (some models use heavy prompt caching so kv penalty differs).
Alex P: agree. I'll open an RFC and a small roll patch to the kernel-selector.
Jonah R: also we should add a microbench for kv-prefetch latency and include it in autotune score. current autotune only measures pure throughput.
Mira T: adding that to my list.
CI-bot: perf run completed: perf/longseq/forced-highocc/2248883331 -> 2248883392: 99p -7.4%, median -0.6%, cost -3.1%
Sreisha: :thumbsup: let's do staged canary tomorrow 04:00 UTC, notify infra and oncall.
Alex P: will draft rollout plan and the selector patch. thanks all.
